chief_complaint: sudden severe generalized abdominal pain with guarding
hpi_details: A 56-year-old female presents to the emergency department with sudden onset of severe, generalized abdominal pain with guarding, which began abruptly and has remained constant since onset.
ideas: She thinks she has a violent bout of food poisoning or that severe trapped gas is tearing through her stomach.
concerns: She is worried that an internal organ burst open and that a deadly blood infection will take her life before her family arrives.
expectations: She hopes to get immediate intravenous pain relief and a definitive scan to determine if she needs surgery right away.

investigation_events.title: Urgent upright chest radiograph
investigation_events.availability_message: The urgent chest radiograph is now available; IV fluids, antibiotics, and emergency surgical consultation should not be delayed.

results.value: Free subdiaphragmatic intraperitoneal air, greatest beneath the right hemidiaphragm

clinical_knowledge.topic: Perforated Peptic Ulcer evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Perforated Peptic Ulcer is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management for Perforated Peptic Ulcer emphasizes emergent laparotomy with Graham patch repair and IV antibiotics, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.

common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Perforated Peptic Ulcer.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Acute pancreatitis without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Board-like rigidity — surgical emergency.

Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

teaching.one_liner: A hole through the stomach or duodenal wall spills contents into the peritoneum, causing sudden, severe, generalized abdominal pain with guarding.

must_ask.say: Did the pain start suddenly and become severe right away?
Do you take pain relievers regularly, or have you had ulcers before?
Does the pain spread to your shoulder?
Does moving make the pain worse?

history.answer: Doctor, my entire stomach suddenly felt like it was tearing apart a few hours ago, and it hurts so much that I can't even move.
It hit me out of nowhere about three hours ago, like a sudden explosion, and it has stayed terrible ever since.
It began right in the upper middle part of my stomach, but within minutes it spread across my whole belly.
I feel an ache shooting up toward my right shoulder, but nothing going down into my groin.
It is a constant, sharp, burning and tearing pain, not like crampy stomach aches.
It is a solid 10 out of 10. It is the worst pain I have ever felt in my life.
Any tiny movement, coughing, or even taking a deep breath makes it excruciating; staying completely still helps a little.
I have had mild burning indigestion off and on for a few months, but never anything even close to this horrible pain.
I felt very sick to my stomach and threw up a little bit of clear fluid once, but there was no blood or dark coffee-ground vomit.
I have not had a bowel movement or passed gas since this agonizing pain started.
My stool was normal brown yesterday, and I have never noticed black tarry or bright red bloody stools.
I feel sweaty and cold, but I haven't noticed any shivering or high fever.
No, my eyes and skin look their normal color, and my urine has not been dark or tea-colored.
No, I have no pain or burning when I urinate, and no blood in my urine.
I feel faint and weak because the pain is so overwhelming, but I haven't blacked out or fainted.
No, I do not have any vaginal bleeding or unusual discharge.
I don't have chest tightness or heart pain, but I can only take shallow breaths because breathing deep hurts my belly.
I had a light bowl of vegetable soup about an hour before this started; nothing greasy or heavy.
I take over-the-counter ibuprofen every few days for back pain and headaches, sometimes on an empty stomach.
No, I have never had an irregular heartbeat, atrial fibrillation, or any blood vessel blockages.
I don't have high blood pressure, diabetes, liver problems, or any major chronic medical conditions.
I have never had any surgeries and have never been hospitalized.
I do not take any daily prescription medications, just the over-the-counter pain relievers I mentioned.
I don't have any known allergies to medicines or foods.
No, I have never smoked cigarettes.
I only have a glass of wine once or twice a month at social gatherings.
I went through menopause about five years ago, so my periods stopped, and there is no chance I could be pregnant.
I work as an administrative clerk in an office, and I live at home with my husband.
There is no family history of stomach cancer, aneurysms, or sudden digestive emergencies.
I thought maybe I ate something toxic or had severe gas trapped inside that's ripping my stomach apart.
I'm terrified that something inside me burst open and that I might not survive this before my family can get here.
I just need something strong for this unbearable agony right now, and I want a scan to tell me if I have to go straight into surgery.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 130/80 mmHg, pulse 104 beats/min, respiratory rate 22 breaths/min, body temperature 37.3°C, SpO2 98% on room air.
Ill-appearing, lying completely still on the stretcher with knees slightly bent in severe acute distress, avoiding any movement.
Conjunctivae are pink without pallor; sclerae are clear without jaundice.
Tachycardic with regular rhythm, normal S1 and S2, no heart murmurs, rubs, or gallops.
Bilateral lung sounds are clear to auscultation with shallow breaths due to abdominal discomfort; no wheezing or crackles.
Abdomen is flat, not visibly distended, moving minimally with breathing; no surgical scars, discoloration, or visible pulsations.
Bowel sounds are markedly hypoactive to nearly absent across all four quadrants.
Severe tenderness on light percussion across the entire abdomen, with resonant tympanitic sound and diminished hepatic dullness.
Severe diffuse tenderness across all four quadrants with involuntary muscular rigidity and board-like guarding.
Severe, excruciating generalized rebound tenderness throughout the entire abdomen.
Severe generalized abdominal wall rigidity prevents isolated focal assessment beneath the right costal margin.
Severe diffuse abdominal guarding and tenderness make focal McBurney localization impossible.
No tenderness upon gentle percussion at either costovertebral angle.
No masses, normal sphincter tone, no gross blood on examining glove, but significant anterior peritoneal tenderness is noted.
